about: Records of the learn-from-failure loop (ebllm.bllm.selfmod): each attempt, the diagnosis of a failure, the rule it changed and the outcome of the retry. The construction, seed and Hodge runs are this engine's own; the other runs were logged by the attacks that used it on 19 October 2026.

runs.title: The seed conjecture for reflexive polytopes, 19 October 2026

records.evidence: of 400 reflexive 3-polytopes, 7 have no reflexive vertex deletion and 237 have a cover that is not a vertex deletion

change.old: delete a vertex and keep the hull of the other lattice points
change.new: a cover, found as the cut of P by a half-space <x,q> >= -1 at a dual lattice point q
change.improves: covers found (vertex deletion misses one on 237 of 400 polytopes)

records.failed_part: cuts at dual points of gauge 2
records.evidence: the cuts give the wrong set of covers for 73 of 400 polytopes

change.old: dual lattice points of gauge 2
change.new: every dual point allowed by the dual volume bound of Balletti, Kasprzyk and Nill and the facet condition, branching where a cut is not reflexive
change.improves: polytopes with the right set of covers (327 of 400)

records.evidence: the covers agree with the known order on 400 of 400 three-dimensional polytopes; the four-dimensional list has 473,800,776 polytopes

change.old: compute a descent of each polytope
change.new: bound every descent by the lattice points of the polytope and of its dual, read once from the list
change.improves: polytopes with a proved bound on every descent (none)

records.evidence: every descent has at most min(|P| - 6, 680 - |P*|) steps, at most 654 over all 473,800,776 polytopes
the longest chain of point-count pairs with |P| falling and |P*| rising has 348 steps, from (521, 22); every descent has at most 348 steps
162,328,050 polytopes have a counting bound above 40; certifying each needs a descent or an exact depth, about 3 minutes for the largest

change.old: certify a descent of every polytope
change.new: certify descents of the extreme polytopes only, and bound the constant from below by exact breadth-first depths
change.improves: certified upper and lower bounds on the sharp constant

records.failed_part: exact depths of the largest polytopes
records.evidence: a certified descent of 38 steps from the 680-point simplex; exact depths 4 and 9 at its polytopes with 15 and 20 points, so the constant is at least 9

change.old: one certified descent of the 680-point simplex
change.new: exact depths at the polytopes along that descent
change.improves: the bound on the depth of the 680-point simplex (38)

records.failed_part: exact depths near the top of the pair bound
records.evidence: the polytope at step 27 has exact depth 9, so the 680-point simplex has depth at most 36; depth adds under free sums, so the sum of a 3-polytope of depth 11 with a segment gives a constant of at least 11

change.old: exact depths along the listed descent of the 680-point simplex
change.new: exact depths below the skew bipyramids with 37 points, from complete cover lists
change.improves: the lower bound on the sharp constant (11, from free sums)

records.failed_part: the gap between the two bounds
records.evidence: two skew bipyramids P_1, P_2 with 37 points have depth exactly 22 (a certificate of 5,592 polytopes with complete cover lists), so the constant is at least 22; a unimodular map carries P_1 onto step 10 of the descent of the 680-point simplex, so that simplex has depth at most 32

change.old: one listed descent of the 680-point simplex
change.new: descend from step 9 of that descent through complete covers, taking at each step the cover of least greedy rank
change.improves: the bound on the depth of the 680-point simplex (32)

records.evidence: a descent of 22 complete covers from step 9 (from 44 to 19 lattice points) gives depth at most 31 for the 680-point simplex; the sharp constant lies between 22 and 348

change.old: exact depths of single polytopes
change.new: certify every polytope of the list at depth at most 50 by chains of cuts, in shards on separate runners
change.improves: row groups of the list certified at depth at most 50

runs.title: The Hodge conjecture at E_0^6 and the chain for sqrt 10, 19 October 2026

records.failed_part: the sixfold Massey product m_6 on the chain of length six
records.evidence: for L^1[-2], L^2[-1], L^3[0], L^4[1] the isolated blocks are 0 and the Euler characteristic is -17665, so counting decides nothing, and the product needs an A-infinity model in theta functions that the library does not have

change.old: count the isolated Ext blocks, then the ranks of the Massey products along the closed chains
change.new: first find the threefold pieces that lie on no closed chain with a nonzero cochain on all but one step, and compare the parity of shift the chains reach with the parity the Chern character forces
change.improves: configurations of family (a) decided (every one with at most five line bundles, for any twists, against none)

records.evidence: every convolution with at most five line bundles fails (experiments/hodge/C1_chains.md, Theorem 6); with two line bundles at one shift the Maurer-Cartan component has a second path, and chains with two runs through threefolds appear

change.old: a chain through a threefold acts when its cochain is nonzero on all but one step
change.new: a zero step beside a nonzero step that is the only path between two line bundles carries no deformation (Lemma 7); search every interval of shifts (Lemma 8)
change.improves: configurations of family (a) decided (at most seven line bundles, against five)

records.evidence: every convolution with at most seven line bundles fails (experiments/hodge/C8_chains.md, Theorem 9); with eight, 31 shift patterns such as the Koszul tower carry live chains of both parities, every Maurer-Cartan component between line bundles two shifts apart has two paths, and the decision needs the ranks of the products along the runs

records.failed_part: the chain S -> Y <- S' through symplectic quotients of orders 2 and 5
records.evidence: the coinvariant lattice of an automorphism of order five has rank 16, so S' has transcendental rank at most 5, while real multiplication by Q(sqrt 10) needs rank at least 6

change.old: admit a chain whose multiplier is right modulo squares
change.new: also require that every surface of the chain can carry the endomorphism field: transcendental rank at least 3[E:Q] against the rank each symplectic quotient allows
change.improves: chain candidates rejected at admission instead of left open

runs.title: Simple zeros on the critical line, 19 October 2026

records.evidence: the claimed bound X^(2+eps)/H on the Liouville correlations E_2(X,H) is false: E_2 is about XH, and at X = 4,000,000, H = X^0.8 the claim is too small by a factor 8498

change.old: accept a bound on the Liouville correlations from a source
change.new: reject any bound below the random-model size, the square root of X for each shift
change.improves: false correlation bounds rejected before use

records.evidence: Nyman-Beurling completeness is equivalent to the hypothesis; the quasi-Riemann hypothesis clears only Re s > 7/8; proportion theorems cannot exclude a set of density zero off the line
records.note: the attack moved to the proportion of the zeros that are simple and on the line

records.target: Proportion of simple zeros on the line
records.evidence: three-point data lift the ceiling of the linear program from 68.18% to 70.9%, but the dual certificate uses the cubic term with the sign that off-line pairs exploit; zero-density estimates control only triples worth 0.0002 to 0.0013

change.old: pair and triple data on every configuration
change.new: higher-order data only where off-line zeros are provably rare, checked against a zero-density estimate
change.improves: the part of the ceiling that can be proved

records.target: Proportion of simple zeros on the line
records.failed_part: a model of off-line pairs with cosh weights
records.evidence: calibrated against the known theorem the model gave 0.584, below the proved 0.6725

change.old: read the optimum of a relaxation
change.new: calibrate every relaxation against a proved theorem before reading it
change.improves: relaxations that reproduce the proved 0.6725

records.target: Proportion of simple zeros on the line
records.evidence: multistart minima gave 0.004746 where the true minimum is 0.004684, and then 0.004629

change.old: the least value found by multistart
change.new: a constant only after a rigorous branch and bound has failed to beat it, restarting from the box where it fails
change.improves: constants that survive certification

records.target: Proportion of simple zeros on the line
records.evidence: it saturates near 67.30%: a Gershgorin tail majorant bounds the overlap eigenvalues by 2.5 and misses the eigenvalue lemma

change.old: a Gershgorin tail bound
change.new: a majorant fitted to the weight: the Fejér kernel, with spectrum exactly [-d, d], is diagonal on d-separated points and needs no tail
change.improves: the bound on the overlap eigenvalues (2.5)

records.target: Proportion of simple zeros on the line
records.evidence: the Fejér majorant bounds the eigenvalues by 1.979 at separation 0.55, and an eight-zero window certified by branch and bound (10,039,560,518 nodes, four times) gives more than 67.311% of the zeros simple and on the line; a pair sum cut at a few hundred neighbours reads the limit of the method too low by about 0.00005

change.old: the pair sum over a few hundred neighbours
change.new: periodic chains summed over all pairs, which cap every window and weight below 0.67357
change.improves: windows started that can pass the record

records.note: in the certificate an idle thread takes half of a busy thread's stack of boxes; the nine-zero window is running

typed crossing closed 128 composites of corners, normal forms and the centre, tested on the 39,322 primes p = 3 mod 4 below 1,000,000: 112 refuted because a normal form does not separate classes, 8 by a collision of centre triples at p = 531359, 1 empty; 7 accepted

runs.title: Union-closed families at the entropy limit, 19 October 2026

records.evidence: the entropy method cannot pass Moffat's ceiling C* = 0.38288525996

change.old: search for an improvement
change.new: look up the known ceilings of the method first
change.improves: searches started beyond a known ceiling

records.evidence: the conjecture that tight families have 2^k sets implies Frankl's, so it is no shortcut; it holds on all 2,771,104 union-closed families on at most five elements

change.old: a shortcut through tight families
change.new: attain the ceiling exactly: tangency, positivity of the Hessian and an interval cover
change.improves: a proved bound at the ceiling (none before)

records.evidence: some element lies in a fraction at least C* of the sets of every union-closed family, and at least C* + ln^2(2N-1)/(128 N^2 ln^2 N) when there are N sets
records.note: the entropy method stops at C*

records.evidence: its kill at level 15 uses the odd factors of K+1; at K = 15, K+1 = 16 has none, and lifts with two odd speeds and thirteen divisible by 32 persisted at the prime 179

change.old: the odd factors of K+1 (Allikvere, Lemma 4.6)
change.new: a shift lemma for powers of two: with d = 2^j dividing the level and g_i = gcd(d, v_i), a lift has a lonely time when the speeds not divisible by d satisfy sum g_i ceil(2(d/g_i)/(K+1)) < d
change.improves: rows settled at the prime 179 (stalled)

records.evidence: the prime 179 runs at about 350 times the old speed; an independent brute-force checker agrees on 3,898 rows

change.old: expand every lift bit pattern
change.new: expand only the canonical patterns, each weighted by a product of binomials, since equal coordinates are interchangeable
change.improves: run time at identical output (about four times less)

records.evidence: at the prime 37 the rows with six or seven speeds in one class form a 2-adic staircase (2-adic valuations 0, 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6) that neither the binary cascade nor the shift lemma settles

change.old: every prime
change.new: when K+1 is a power of two, only primes of at least 89
change.improves: rows left open by the staircase

records.note: the full run needs 4,000 to 7,000 CPU-hours
